inspiration.observed_pattern: Aggregate pushdown cases use SUM(DISTINCT ...) both as a scalar aggregate and alongside a join, grouping expression, and NULL-aware filter.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an original campaign-spend report. A LEFT JOIN groups spend by campaign and projects ordinary SUM, SUM(DISTINCT), and COUNT(DISTINCT) together; duplicate amounts must contribute once to the distinct total, while NULL-only and NULL-containing campaigns exercise aggregate NULL semantics without copying the source schema or rows.

fixture_notes: Campaign 10 has two 125-cent charges and one 250-cent charge, so SUM counts 500 while SUM(DISTINCT) counts 375 and COUNT(DISTINCT) counts two values. Campaign 20 has duplicate 300-cent charges plus one NULL. Campaign 30 has no spend rows and must retain NULL SUM results through the LEFT JOIN.
determinism_notes: Campaign IDs and spend IDs are fixed; the grouped report is ordered by the unique campaign ID. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE campaigns (campaign_id INT PRIMARY KEY, campaign_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE campaign_spend (spend_id INT PRIMARY KEY, campaign_id INT NOT NULL, channel VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, amount_cents INT NULL)

INSERT INTO campaign_spend VALUES (1, 10, 'search', 125), (2, 10, 'social', 125), (3, 10, 'video', 250), (4, 10, 'display', NULL), (5, 20, 'search', 300), (6, 20, 'social', 300), (7, 20, 'video', NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name, SUM(s.amount_cents) AS total_cents, SUM(DISTINCT s.amount_cents) AS distinct_cents, COUNT(DISTINCT s.amount_cents) AS distinct_amounts FROM campaigns c LEFT JOIN campaign_spend s ON s.campaign_id = c.campaign_id GROUP BY c.campaign_id, c.campaign_name ORDER BY c.campaign_id
